skill.name: laravel-specialist
skill.description: Guides Laravel 10+ development for Eloquent models, API resources, queues, Livewire components, Sanctum authentication, and tests.
skill.summary: Build Laravel applications with Eloquent, APIs, queues, Livewire, authentication, and focused test coverage.
skill.author: jeffallan

security_audit.summary: The static malware indicators are false positives caused by Laravel documentation examples, Markdown formatting, and sample URLs. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or shell execution intent was found. One semantic issue remains: a Livewire delete example omits an authorization check before deleting a post.

remediation.issue: Destructive Livewire action deletes a post by ID without authorization.
remediation.suggestion: Add policy authorization before deletion, use findOrFail, and test ownership checks for the delete action.

semantic_findings.title: Missing Authorization in Livewire Delete Example
semantic_findings.description: The Livewire event example deletes a Post from a supplied ID without a policy check. If copied into an app, a user could delete another user's record.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The snippet directly calls Post::find($postId)->delete() in a public component action. The surrounding section demonstrates events, not authorization, so the unsafe pattern could be reused.

content.value_statement: Laravel teams need consistent patterns for models, APIs, queues, Livewire, and tests. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused Laravel implementation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Designs Eloquent models with relationships, scopes, casts, observers, and eager loading patterns.
Builds REST API routes, controllers, form requests, API resources, middleware, and versioned routes.
Creates queue jobs, batches, middleware, failed job handling, Horizon setup, and queue configuration examples.
Implements Livewire components with forms, validation, events, loading states, traits, and authorization examples.
Writes Laravel feature, unit, database, API, authentication, factory, mocking, and Pest testing guidance.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a running Laravel application by itself.
It targets Laravel 10+ and PHP 8.2+, so older projects may need adaptation.
It does not replace project-specific security review, authorization design, or database tuning.
It may need current Laravel documentation for new framework features after publication.

use_cases.title: Implement a Laravel Feature
use_cases.description: Create models, migrations, controllers, resources, services, and tests for a new product feature.

use_cases.title: Improve API Quality
use_cases.description: Refine routes, form requests, API resources, middleware, pagination, and versioning for a Laravel API.

use_cases.title: Stabilize Queues and Livewire
use_cases.description: Add queue jobs, Horizon monitoring, Livewire validation, authorization, and tests for interactive workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for an Eloquent model and migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Laravel model and migration for a blog post. Include fillable fields, casts, relationships, and a simple feature test.

prompt_templates.title: Build an API Endpoint
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for REST API implementation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a Laravel API endpoint for posts. Include routes, controller actions, form requests, API resources, pagination, and authorization notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Queued Processing
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Laravel queue workflow for image processing. Include jobs, retries, failed job handling, Horizon monitoring, and tests.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Laravel Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for system design and code review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Laravel feature plan for scalability, security, testing, queues, Eloquent performance, and Livewire behavior. Recommend concrete changes.

output_examples.input: Build a posts API with categories and authors.
output: A clear model and relationship plan for posts, users, categories, and comments.
A route and controller outline with request validation and API resources.
A focused test plan for creation, filtering, permissions, and pagination.

output_examples.input: Add a background job for publishing notifications.
output: A queued job design with retry, timeout, and failure handling guidance.
A dispatch strategy that avoids slow web requests.
A testing approach using queue fakes and failure cases.
A component structure with validation, authorization, and loading states.
A template plan for inputs, errors, and save behavior.
A test outline for valid updates, invalid data, and denied access.

best_practices: Load only the relevant reference file before changing a Laravel feature.
Pair implementation guidance with validation, authorization, and focused tests.
Review generated examples against the target Laravel version and project conventions.
anti_patterns: Do not copy examples without adding project-specific authorization rules.
Do not use queue or CORS examples as production configuration without review.
Do not mix controller, model, and service responsibilities in one layer.

faq.question: Which Laravel versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Laravel 10+ with PHP 8.2+ patterns and modern framework conventions.

faq.question: Can it help with Eloquent performance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers eager loading, scopes, relationships, casts, events, and query optimization patterns.

faq.question: Does it include API guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers routes, controllers, form requests, API resources, middleware, pagination, and versioning.

faq.question: Does it support Livewire work?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes components, forms, validation, events, loading states, traits, and authorization examples.

faq.question: Can it design queue systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers jobs, retries, batching, middleware, failed jobs, workers, Horizon, and configuration.

faq.question: Does it replace a security review?
faq.answer: No. Review generated Laravel code for project-specific authorization, secret handling, and deployment settings.
